Creative Machines · the eval layer

How it knows the output is good — before you spend on it.

There's no single right answer for a creative, so you can't QA it like normal software. So every output is scored on explicit dimensions, and an independent critic kills the generic ones before they ship.

The judge still pushes — even on a pass

Flagged a real weakness: the three angles were one promise across audiences, leaving two open lanes untested. Not a rubber stamp.

2

The critic catching a weak one — before a rupee is spent

DailyObjects (phone cases). The critic never sees the writer's reasoning. It only tries to kill.

Round 1 · reject all

5 concepts in — 5 killed

Swap test failed — a rival could run them unchanged
Category-look — the tasteful "case on a surface" every brand uses
Obvious-first-idea — the take a junior writes first
Critic: "A five-take set that never once makes the claim physical in an invented scene cannot hold a scroll-stopping click it never attempted." → regenerate.
Round 2 · winner

"The Keynote"

Swap test passed — the one claim no rival can make
A made world — the case 40ft tall on a product-launch stage
Welded to the brand — "the name is the whole point"
Critic: "Strip the brand and the take stops existing… the only claim in the batch literally no other company can make. The weld is to the name, not the category."

Then it checks the actual picture — the vision-gate

The winner gets rendered. A second pass re-reads the finished image against the plan. Look at the headline on the left — you can see it caught the problem with its own eyes.

v1 · gate failed

The presenter silhouette landed on top of the headline — "keynote" reads "_ynote". Caught automatically.

v2 · gate passed

One targeted retry. Headline fully legible, silhouette moved clear of the text. Ships.

You can't QA a creative like software — there's no single right answer. So you score it on dimensions and let an independent critic kill the generic ones. That's the part that decides whether a system like this is trustworthy or not.
